profile.address: One Wilshire Building, 624 South Grand Avenue, Los Angeles, CA 90017
profile.reading: GI Partners owns One Wilshire, a 30 story, 664,000 square foot office tower at 624 South Grand Avenue, Los Angeles, California 90017, built in 1966 to a design by Skidmore, Owings and Merrill after construction began in 1964, per Wikipedia's own article on the building. Originally leased primarily to law firms through the early 1990s, the building's tenant base shifted to telecommunications companies drawn partly by proximity to a nearby AT&T switching center. A meet-me room built on the fourth floor around 1992 let tenants directly interconnect their networks, and by 2008 Wired reported it held the world's most densely populated meet-me room, with roughly 260 interconnected internet service providers. One Wilshire changed hands several times before GI Partners acquired it in 2013 for 437.5 million dollars, following S. Jon Kreedman and Company's original 1960s development, a 2001 sale to Carlyle Group for 119 million dollars, and a 2007 sale to Hines Real Estate Investment Trust for 287 million dollars. By 2013 the building ranked among the world's top three telecommunications data centers, per Wikipedia, serving as a primary fiber optic terminus between Asia and North America; submarine cable connections routed through the building were reported to carry roughly one third of internet traffic between the United States and Asia. As of 2015 the building housed more than 300 tenants, including CoreSite Realty, Verizon, Amazon Web Services, and Netflix, several of which are separately profiled elsewhere in this registry. One Wilshire's own site describes the building as the most vital carrier hotel in the western United States. GI Partners, a private investment firm founded in 2001 and headquartered in San Francisco managing more than 40 billion dollars across private equity, real estate, and data infrastructure strategies, functions here as an institutional owner and landlord of carrier hotel real estate rather than a colocation brand marketing directly to end customers.

profile.reading: This facility, at 22262 Cloud Plaza, Sterling, Virginia 20166, at the southwest corner of Waxpool Road and Route 28 in Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, is a 238,000 square foot, 46 megawatt critical power data center that GI Partners acquired a majority stake in on May 19, 2022, per industry publication Dgtl Infra, paying 709 million dollars, or roughly 15.4 million dollars per megawatt, through an entity called GI TC Loudoun LLC. The seller, Sentinel Data Centers, specifically an entity called Sentinel Ashburn II LLC owned by Rabina Properties, retained a minority stake in the property after the sale. The building was delivered and fully commissioned by 2019 and sits on 23.8 acres of land adjacent to Vantage Data Centers' Ashburn campus, tracked elsewhere in this registry. Dgtl Infra describes the facility's tenant as a global technology firm functioning as a credit tenant, meaning an investment grade rated company under a long-term lease, consistent with GI Partners' own broader description of this and related Ashburn area holdings as fully leased, credit tenant properties acquired as institutional real estate investments rather than operated as a directly marketed colocation brand. GI Partners, a private investment firm founded in 2001 and headquartered in San Francisco managing more than 40 billion dollars across private equity, real estate, and data infrastructure strategies, has made multiple such acquisitions in Northern Virginia's Data Center Alley, including a separate fully leased facility at 43915 Devin Shafron Drive in Ashburn acquired in April 2023, and has signed a major lease with DataBank, another operator already profiled in this registry, for a new Ashburn, Virginia data center. GI Partners' broader Tech and Science real estate portfolio spans 49 properties totaling 10.1 million square feet across 12 markets.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] GI Partners is a private investment firm founded in 2001 and headquartered in San Francisco, with additional offices in New York, Dallas, Chicago, Greenwich, Scottsdale, and London. The firm manages more than 40 billion dollars in capital across private equity, real estate, and data infrastructure investment strategies, and functions as an institutional acquirer and owner of data center real estate rather than as an operating brand that markets colocation directly to end customers. GI Partners has made multiple acquisitions in Northern Virginias Data Center Alley, including the Sentinel data center in Sterling, Virginia, purchased from Starwood Capital, and a fully leased facility at 43915 Devin Shafron Drive in Ashburn, acquired April 18, 2023, offering 9 megawatts of critical power with room to expand, 100 percent leased to two credit-worthy tenants within a 98-acre campus that has been institutionally maintained since its original 2010 construction. The firm has also signed a major lease with DataBank, another operator already profiled in this registry, for a new Ashburn, Virginia data center. GI Partners broader Tech and Science real estate portfolio spans 49 properties totaling 10.1 million square feet across 12 markets. Because GI Partners operates as an investor and landlord across multiple Northern Virginia properties rather than a single named facility, this registrys one Virginia facility record for the company is treated as representing this broader investment relationship rather than a single confirmed address.
